parent_v18.key_result: source placement, not count alone, determined a coverage-insurance tradeoff

scientific_question: After one source population is lost from a three-source EOG network, does restoring source count with a replacement population restore the original distributional function, or does replacement placement create persistent differences in coverage, redundancy and provenance?

latent_landscapes.reuse: the exact 384 v18 directed truth graphs, A/B permissibility fields, outlet definitions and eligible source registry
latent_landscapes.starting_networks: the frozen v18 three-source clustered and dispersed source sets

loss_event.rule: remove the source whose loss gives the smallest remaining union-reachable node count; ties broken by node ID
loss_event.interpretation: worst coverage shock under the frozen three-source network

replacement_candidate_pool.eligible: all frozen v18 eligible source candidates excluding the two surviving sources and excluding the lost source itself
replacement_candidate_pool.no_candidate_rule: row/design is non-estimable for turnover and retained as such

replacement_strategies.local_near_lost: candidate minimizing Euclidean distance to the lost source; ties by node ID
replacement_strategies.clustered_near_survivors: candidate minimizing minimum Euclidean distance to either surviving source; ties by node ID
replacement_strategies.dispersed_far_from_survivors: candidate maximizing minimum Euclidean distance to the surviving source set; ties by node ID

metrics.multi_source_overlap: fraction of union-reachable nodes reachable from at least two sources
metrics.worst_source_loss_retention: minimum remaining-union/original-union ratio after deleting any one source from the replacement network
metrics.exclusive_source_fraction: fraction of union-reachable nodes reachable from exactly one source
metrics.coverage_recovery_fraction: (replacement coverage - post-loss coverage)/(original coverage - post-loss coverage), defined only when original coverage exceeds post-loss coverage
metrics.insurance_recovery_fraction: replacement worst-source-loss retention / original pre-loss worst-source-loss retention when the denominator is positive

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one eligible row/design has different union coverage among the three replacement strategies despite all returning to three sources.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if all strategies always give identical coverage after replacement.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: For both starting designs, pooled mean replacement coverage is strictly larger for dispersed_far_from_survivors than for clustered_near_survivors.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED separately for any starting design whose contrast is <=0.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: For both starting designs, pooled mean multi-source overlap is strictly larger for clustered_near_survivors than for dispersed_far_from_survivors.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED separately for any starting design whose contrast is <=0.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: For both starting designs, pooled mean worst-source-loss retention is strictly larger for clustered_near_survivors than for dispersed_far_from_survivors.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED separately for any starting design whose contrast is <=0.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one row/design/strategy reaches strictly more nodes after replacement than the original three-source network did.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if replacement coverage never exceeds original coverage.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one eligible row/design retains replacement coverage below the original three-source coverage under all three replacement strategies.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if every row/design has at least one replacement that fully restores original coverage.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one row/design has dispersed replacement with higher coverage and clustered replacement with higher worst-source-loss retention.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if no post-turnover coverage-insurance tradeoff occurs.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Every estimable replacement network contains exactly three unique sources and the replacement is never the lost source.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: Any violation is an implementation/theory failure.

secondary_outputs: recovery fractions by starting placement design
fraction of rows where local replacement is best for coverage or insurance
effect modification by barrier density, autocorrelation and neighbourhood
frequency with which each replacement strategy restores or exceeds original coverage
change in exclusive-source fraction as a provenance proxy
claim_boundary: This is structural source-network turnover, not demographic extinction or establishment probability.
Replacement strategies are geometry rules in synthetic landscapes, not direct translocation prescriptions.
Source-loss and replacement happen on a static directed transition graph; no ecological succession is modeled.
Coverage recovery does not imply abundance or long-term persistence.
stop_rules: Do not change the worst-source loss rule after scoring.
Do not allow the lost source itself as a replacement after scoring.
Do not add an oracle best-replacement treatment after scoring.
Do not change replacement geometry rules after scoring.
